Player identification in field sports integrates multiple modalities—facial features, jersey numbers, and positional tracking—into a unified probabilistic framework. Each modality contributes to a composite likelihood function that updates belief about player identity over time. Facial recognition provides static identity anchors, while bib numbers offer deterministic labeling. Positional tracking enables dynamic state transitions in a spatiotemporal graph. The system's dual nature lies in its ability to operate both in offline batch mode (for post-game analysis) and online streaming mode (for real-time coaching). Failure modes include occlusion, poor image quality, and misclassification due to similarity in appearance or number visibility. These are mitigated through ensemble methods and redundancy across modalities. The core mathematical structure is a Bayesian network where nodes represent player identities and edges encode temporal dependencies and cross-modal correlations.
